name: OpenRouter hosted API router
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, representative model meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct ROUTED TO GROQ, re-verified 2026-10-17. OpenRouter is a router, not a hoster: the same model id fans out to DeepInfra, Novita, AkashML, Parasail, Cloudflare, SambaNova, Groq, CoreWeave, Google Vertex and Together, each with its own upstream price that OpenRouter passes through. The 2026-10-17 provider table still spans $0.10/$0.32 (DeepInfra Turbo) to $1.04/$1.04 (Together). price_input/price_output here stay the GROQ row ($0.59/$0.79) — the highest-throughput backend — not the floor. The page headline still prints the floor route ($0.10/$0.32) as 'the' price; that is a different claim and is named here rather than written into the scalar fields. Cache-read on Groq is still $0.295. SambaNova's list $0.60/$1.20 now renders struck through next to a 25% off badge at $0.45/$0.90; that discount is recorded on svc-sambanova-cloud, not folded into this Groq-row price. No single 'OpenRouter price' exists for a model; quote provider+model or nothing.
notes: OpenRouter's own routing telemetry is the measurement: its model pages publish per-provider P50 latency, throughput and uptime measured over real routed traffic. Re-read 2026-10-17, Groq row on llama-3.3-70b-instruct: 0.50s P50 latency, 198 tok/s, 100.00% uptime. That replaces the 2026-10-16 Groq row (0.52s, 193 tok/s, 100% uptime) and the 2026-10-14 row (0.40s, 233 tok/s). Same source, same model, one day later, slightly faster than yesterday and still ~15% slower than the Oct-14 snapshot. Both earlier pairs stay in this note so the drift is visible. measurement_source 'self' means measured-by-the-service-itself over production traffic, a different claim from both a vendor marketing number and the Artificial Analysis medians stored on the individual provider records (Groq's own record carries the AA figure of 305.7 tok/s, not this one). context_window is per-model-per-provider; 131072 is the llama-3.3-70b figure. Balanced/Nitro/Floor/Exacto routing modes pick different providers for the same request, so 'where does it run' is a routing decision, not a property of the endpoint.
